name: java-vsix-lite
description: Minimal, low-compute Java language support for VS Code (pure-Rust default tier; optional opt-in javac tier).

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The pure-Rust default tier (highlighting, structure, lint, signature IntelliSense) runs in untrusted workspaces — it never executes project code and never touches the network. The optional javac tier, the consent-gated dependency download, and Install Dependencies (which runs the project's Maven/Gradle build scripts) all stay disabled until the workspace is trusted.

java-vsix-lite.server.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `jvl-server` binary. Leave empty to use the bundled binary. The `JVL_SERVER_PATH` environment variable overrides this. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace must never be able to redirect which binary is launched as the language server.

java-vsix-lite.trace.server.description: Trace the JSON-RPC traffic between VS Code and the language server (for debugging).

java-vsix-lite.diagnostics.unresolvedMem.markdownDescription: Report an error for a member access (`obj.foo()`) when the receiver's type **and its entire supertype chain** resolve but declare no such member. Conservative: stays silent whenever resolution is incomplete (an unknown supertype, a missing dependency JAR, generics). On by default; disable if you hit a false positive on a hierarchy the resolver can't fully see.

java-vsix-lite.jdk.home.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a JDK home to use for `Check Project (javac)` (M5.4), tried before `$JAVA_HOME`. Leave empty to use `$JAVA_HOME`. Never downloaded — if neither resolves to a real `javac`, the check fails with a clear error. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace must never be able to point `javac` at a binary it ships.

java-vsix-lite.javac.timeoutSecs.markdownDescription: How long `Check Project (javac)` (M5.4) waits before killing `javac`, in seconds. Clamped to 10–600.

java-vsix-lite.javac.checkOnSave.markdownDescription: Run `Check Project (javac)` automatically when the project loads and after saving a Java file (M8b), publishing real compiler errors to Problems. Debounced, one run at a time, and silent (no pop-ups — results land in Problems only). Only active in a **trusted** workspace, because it spawns the JDK's `javac`; in an untrusted workspace saves never trigger it. Uses the same JDK resolution and timeout as the manual command.

java-vsix-lite.dependencies.repository.markdownDescription: Base URL of the Maven repository to download missing dependencies from (M8f), e.g. an internal Artifactory/Nexus proxy in a governed network: `https://artifacts.example.com/maven2`. Empty means Maven Central. Must be a plain `https://` URL — no credentials, query, or fragment; anything else disables downloads rather than silently falling back. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace (repository) must never be able to redirect where your dependency downloads come from. Checksum sidecar verification applies to any repository, unchanged.

java-vsix-lite.maven.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `mvn` executable used by `Install Dependencies (runs build tool)`. Leave empty to use the project's `mvnw` wrapper if present, otherwise `mvn` on `PATH`. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace must never be able to choose which executable is run on your behalf.

java-vsix-lite.gradle.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `gradle` executable used by `Install Dependencies (runs build tool)`. Leave empty to use the project's `gradlew` wrapper if present, otherwise `gradle` on `PATH`. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace must never be able to choose which executable is run on your behalf.

java-vsix-lite.dependencies.autoDownload.markdownDescription: What to do when missing dependencies are detected (M7), in a trusted workspace: `prompt` asks once per session with a Download / Always / Never choice; `always` downloads silently from then on (same HTTPS + checksum verification, Maven Central only, as `Java: Download Missing Dependencies`); `never` disables the automatic check (the manual command still works). Choosing Always or Never from the prompt updates this setting for the current workspace.
